The PR extracts the GitHub Copilot domain allowlist into a shared SDK leaf, applies it to OAuth and model endpoint construction, and normalizes legacy doctor-migrated enterprise domains.

PR surface: Source +12, Tests +125. Total +137 across 6 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current source provides a high-confidence reproduction path from persisted `enterpriseUrl` through automatic OAuth refresh to the bearer-bearing request, and the PR supplies controlled before/after output from the production functions.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): fail closed on unvalidated OAuth enterprise domain
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A legacy `oauth`-typed `github-copilot` auth profile can carry a non-github.com `enterpriseUrl`. On every automatic background token refresh, the built-in GitHub Copilot OAuth provider reconstructs the refresh endpoint from that persisted value and sends the real bearer refresh token to it, with no allowlist anywhere on the path.

Root cause on `origin/main` (`e06b42674b4db8af0677d9d88009555768428223`):

`refreshGitHubCopilotToken` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts` builds the endpoint straight from the raw domain:

```ts
// before
const domain = enterpriseDomain || "github.com";
const urls = getUrls(domain); // https://api.${domain}/copilot_internal/v2/token
// ...
Authorization: `Bearer ${refreshToken}`,
```

The provider hook feeds the persisted field in unchecked (`refreshToken` -> `refreshGitHubCopilotToken(creds.refresh, creds.enterpriseUrl)`), and `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` has the same gap on its enterprise fallback (that URL carries the access token). Two upstream loaders round-trip `enterpriseUrl` verbatim: `coerceLegacyFlatCredential` (doctor `--fix` migration) and `normalizeRawCredentialEntry` (every disk load). The repo already ships a hardened, fail-closed allowlist for exactly this, `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain` (public `github.com` plus `*.ghe.com` tenants only), but the legacy oauth refresh path never calls it.

This is the audited legacy oauth+enterpriseUrl shape only; the shipped provider plugin stores `type: 'token'` credentials and keeps the domain in the allowlisted `githubDomain` config, so it is unaffected. Reachable for upgrade/legacy-state users via `openclaw doctor --fix` or direct tampering of the on-disk store.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix reuses the one canonical allowlist at the URL-building chokepoints so the legacy path fails closed at runtime, and scrubs unsafe values out of persisted state during migration.

- `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain` and its constants move to a new dependency-free leaf `src/plugin-sdk/github-copilot-domain.ts`, re-exported from `provider-auth.ts` so the public SDK surface is unchanged. The leaf exists because `github-copilot.ts` cannot import `provider-auth.ts` (that would close a module cycle `github-copilot -> provider-auth -> auth-profiles/oauth -> llm/oauth registry -> github-copilot`).
- `getUrls` normalizes its domain at entry (covers refresh plus the device/login endpoints). `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` normalizes only its enterprise fallback and only when a value is present, so the no-domain case still returns `api.individual.githubcopilot.com`. `modifyModels` now routes through that hardened chokepoint.
- Doctor `--fix`: `coerceLegacyFlatCredential` normalizes a `github-copilot` credential's `enterpriseUrl` during migration (idempotent: `github.com`/`*.ghe.com` pass through, anything else becomes `github.com`), scoped to that provider so other credentials are untouched.

This closes the P0 egress by reusing shipped hardening and cleans migrated legacy state. Any deeper upgrade-migration or release-behavior policy for already-persisted values is left for maintainer decision. Note this issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`, `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`, and `clawsweeper:needs-security-review`; opening as draft for that review.

## User Impact

Users with a legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth profile carrying a non-allowlisted `enterpriseUrl` no longer leak their bearer refresh/access tokens to that host on background refresh; the token now goes to `github.com` (or a valid `*.ghe.com` tenant). Legitimate public and data-residency GHE users see no behavior change. Fixes #103078.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts` -> 78 pass, including the new allowlist and migration cases (which fail on pristine main and pass with the patch).
- `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files -> clean.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` -> clean (confirms the extracted leaf breaks the cycle and types resolve). The `tsconfig.core.test.json` lane shows only pre-existing `ui/` dependency errors present identically with and without this diff; none in touched files.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: the legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth refresh path sends the bearer refresh token to an attacker-controlled host reconstructed from an unvalidated persisted enterpriseUrl, and doctor migration persists that unsafe value verbatim
Real environment tested: real production functions driven directly on pristine origin/main e06b42674b4db8af0677d9d88009555768428223 and on the patched tree with identical inputs: refreshGitHubCopilotToken and githubCopilotOAuthProvider.refreshToken (src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts), the real doctor migration maybeRepairLegacyFlatAuthProfileStores reading back through loadPersistedAuthProfileStore (src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.ts, src/agents/auth-profiles/persisted.ts), and normalizeGithubCopilotDomain (src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts) for contrast; only the outbound fetch() network call was replaced with a stub that records the request and returns a valid token body, all domain resolution and credential loading ran unmodified
Exact steps or command run after this patch: called refreshGitHubCopilotToken("ghr_real_refresh_token", "attacker.example") and githubCopilotOAuthProvider.refreshToken with a persisted-shaped credential carrying enterpriseUrl "attacker.example", then wrote a legacy flat auth-profiles.json github-copilot oauth entry with enterpriseUrl "attacker.example", drove the real doctor migration, and read the persisted result back
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main e06b42674b)
refreshGitHubCopilotToken request : https://api.attacker.example/copilot_internal/v2/token   Authorization: Bearer ghr_real_refresh_token
provider.refreshToken request     : https://api.attacker.example/copilot_internal/v2/token   Authorization: Bearer ghr_legacy_refresh
doctor-migrated enterpriseUrl     : attacker.example
normalizeGithubCopilotDomain("attacker.example") : github.com

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
refreshGitHubCopilotToken request : https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token         Authorization: Bearer ghr_real_refresh_token
provider.refreshToken request     : https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token         Authorization: Bearer ghr_legacy_refresh
doctor-migrated enterpriseUrl     : github.com
normalizeGithubCopilotDomain("attacker.example") : github.com
```
Observed result after fix: the bearer token that previously went to api.attacker.example now goes to api.github.com, and the migrated enterpriseUrl that was persisted as attacker.example is now stored as github.com; the already-hardened normalizeGithubCopilotDomain returns github.com in both runs, isolating the refresh and migration paths as the ones that changed
What was not tested: no live GitHub Copilot account or real device-code login was exercised; the outbound fetch() was stubbed since sending live bearer credentials to a real third-party host is out of scope for a safe repro; the interactive loginGitHubCopilot flow has no current caller and was not driven end to end
